artworks.title: Antigone Giving Burial to Polynices
artworks.description: Norblin's Prix de Rome canvas shows the handful of dust: Antigone burying Polynices against Creon's ban — the act that defines the Theban sister.

artworks.title: Antigone at the Bedside of Polynices
artworks.description: Benjamin-Constant's Antigone keeps vigil over her brother's corpse — the quiet moment before defiance becomes Sophocles' tragedy.

artworks.title: Antigone
artworks.description: Leighton's solitary Antigone in classical drapery — conscience without Creon or corpse, the sister who chooses the dead over the city's law.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Irene Papas' Antigone buries her brother against Creon's decree — Sophocles filmed in Greece, the sister who chooses the dead over the living law.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's opera, after Cocteau's compression of Sophocles, sets Antigone's defiance in stark modern harmony — the burial as an act of music.

popCulture.title: Antigone (Sophocles play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: The sister who buries her brother against the city's law — still the West's central drama of conscience versus decree.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.description: Oedipus' daughter remains the name for civil disobedience before the grave — dust on Polynices' body.
